demonstrates: Added the first human-facing surface to an MCP proxy that had only ever served machines: a server-rendered, identity-gated page on its own origin, where the authorization question is answered by one selector shared with the index rather than a second lookup, and where the hostname's two required declarations are now bound by a validator that is itself guarded against gaining an unchecked fourth input.

claims.section: A hostname must be declared TWICE, and since 2026-09-11 that IS checked
claims.note: Response to a request carrying the machine-protocol Host header, measured on the live fleet 2026-09-11T04:17Z. A redirect to the identity provider is the correct outcome for that host and is the control the 403 is read against.

claims.section: A hostname must be declared TWICE, and since 2026-09-11 that IS checked
claims.note: Response to a request carrying the dashboard Host header, measured in the same 2026-09-11T04:17Z pair, with the route registered and the boot log confirming it. The DNS-rebinding allowlist refused the request before any handler ran, and named no cause. Every occurrence in the article is this measurement.

claims.section: It is an index and a detail page, not one scroll
claims.note: Status returned for a workspace slug the account has no membership for, and identically for a slug that exists nowhere in the deployment. The symmetry is the claim: the page cannot be used to enumerate which tenants the deployment has.

claims.section: The view model, and what it deliberately does not carry
claims.note: Services that would have required rebuilding had the wiki list been read from the canonical source registry, because reaching it needs a root re-export that moves the shared contract hash. The list was removed the same day (bfdf1436), so this is the cost of a road not taken. Counts services in the cascade, not packages.
